sections.title: Your first week
lines: Pick a starter. Your first expedition always brings back a Zipmouse.
Open the game each day for a Bait allowance, and leet in Discord for a bonus. Spend Bait on treats and lures.
Creatures grow by doing: trips, the dungeon, raids and Workshop jobs. At level 10 one gets its finale ability.
You join the weekly raid automatically. On Sunday evening everyone fights the boss together.
Tap any tag in the game to see what it means.

sections.title: Creatures
lines: Each creature has an element (Tide, Ember, Grove, Spark or Mire) and a role (Setter, Payoff, Guard or Support).
Whatever a creature does earns it experience. A treat (Bait) doubles it for one activity.
Ribbons (made from parts) wait at levels 10 and 20. Many evolve at 15 for Essence, and most pick one of two forms.
Every catch rolls a talent. More talent slots open at higher levels, and the Talent Book keeps old ones.
A duplicate catch is a choice: Teach its talent, Fuse it, Release it for parts, or sometimes Keep it.

sections.title: Combos
lines: The boss carries one mark at a time. Your hits leave it.
Hit a marked boss with the right element (see the Element chart) to set off a reaction.
A reaction deals much more damage and uses up the mark.
Setters swap marks. Put them before the creature that cashes in.
Payoffs hit even harder when they set off a reaction.

sections.title: The raid week
lines: Monday to Friday is Preparation: the new boss is revealed. Set your team and your row.
Friday and Saturday: Phases 1 and 2 play out by themselves.
Each phase needs a share of the boss's HP. The finale needs all of it.
After Phase 1 the boss adapts with a counter-move.
Sunday 20:00: the live finale. The Raid tab shows the exact times.

sections.title: The live finale
lines: The fight plays out round by round, live.
Tap one of your creatures to fire its ability. It lands next round.
Auto fire is on by default: abilities fire by themselves in their round.
Turn Auto fire off to time it yourself. It still fires in the last round.
A warning shows what the boss will do next round.

sections.title: Expeditions
lines: Send a creature out for 2, 6 or 12 hours. Each hour may find creatures, parts, gear or supplies. Longer is better.
Trips are free. Parts are every crafting ingredient: scrap, shards and glimmer. Supplies make a trip better.
Every creature gets better at exploring: ranks, stars for each place and Journal pages.
A finished trip may offer a push-on choice. Safe goals always work. Risky ones can fail.
You start with 1 slot, and more open as your creatures grow. Recall early to keep what the hours so far found.

sections.title: Daily dungeon
lines: One run a day, with a team of three. The day resets at 13:37 server time. A lost first run can be retried once.
Walk a map room by room: fights, elites, mystery rooms and chests. HP carries over. A camp sits halfway.
At the camp, rest, swap a creature or take a keepsake, then push on or head home.
Home keeps your pack. A defeat keeps half, rounded up. Beat the boss to go one depth deeper.
Every 7th depth is a landmark: gear for sure. Daily streaks pay a bonus on the 3rd and 7th day of every 7.

sections.title: Ranks and Festivals
lines: Every boss has a Rank. Each Rank makes the boss stronger.
Win the finale and the server's Rank goes up by 1. Lose and it stays.
Every 5th week is a Festival: an easier boss and extra Essence.
Win a Festival to get its special creature. The pips show where you are in the 5-week season.
Each day has a Boon that helps and, from Rank 3, an Omen that hinders. The wall calendar shows tomorrow's.

sections.title: Rewards
lines: Clear a stage and everyone in the party gets Essence.
Most of it is equal. A share depends on how much you helped: your score.
Win the finale and everyone in the party also gets a gear piece or a blueprint.
Higher Ranks pay more Essence and better gear. Festival weeks pay more Essence.
Essence evolves creatures and pays for Reach crafts. Opening the game and leeting earn Bait.

sections.title: Valley Games
lines: Three silly events a day, four on Wednesdays. A creature enters one; in one, three play as a team.
Enter before the daily reset: only what you enter plays. The show is live a few minutes after it.
Level doesn't matter here; species, element, role and size do. Good fit marks a creature that suits.
The top three win gold, silver and bronze; a winner earns the event's badge, a new best a pin. All earn experience.
The bonus event pays double medal points. Spend them at the Prize Stall on Wednesdays.

sections.title: Gear
lines: Each creature wears a Hat, a Scarf from level 7 and a Charm from level 13, each up to its own level.
Hats and Scarves carry Attack and HP of their own. A Charm carries a fixed line instead.
A Common has 1 line, a Rare 2 and an Epic 3. Lines marked (this item) grow the item's own stats.
The pips show how strong a line rolled; the item's level sets the best. An Ember piece rolls Ember lines more often.
Some lines depend on where a creature stands, fire by chance or react in a fight. Set pieces give a bonus worn together.

sections.title: The Workshop
lines: Creatures work jobs, even while you are away. You can run 2 at once.
Craft from a blueprint you know. A plain craft makes a Common; Reach for a Rare or Epic with Essence.
Dismantle what you do not need for parts and Essence. It can teach you the item's blueprint.
Gear and blueprints come from won finales, expeditions, the dungeon and Festivals.
A creature on a job cannot go on an expedition. It still fights in raids.

example.title: Example: Overload
lines: Splashet is a Tide Setter. Its hit leaves the boss Soaked.
Stormray is a Spark Payoff. Its hit sets off Overload!
The hit deals much more damage, and the Soaked mark is used up.
